outcome: Oracle's declared infrastructure ownership is reconciled with physical package/module ownership: concrete Oracle resolution code moves behind an infrastructure-owned package boundary without introducing an unproven generic resolver framework or changing current Backend/QA semantics.
currentProblem: Living architecture says Oracle is infrastructure and not Agentic Application/Core, but current implementation is physically colocated in packages/agentic-system/src/oracle.js. The temporary Wave-A colocation became persistent and closure machinery never checked logical ownership against source/package ownership.
constraints: Preserve current resolveBackendContext/resolveQaContext behavior and application-owned schemas.
Oracle must be physically owned outside @exharness/agentic-system after delivery.
Do not invent Resolver<T>, provider registry, lifecycle framework, retrieval engine or cache abstraction merely to justify extraction.

Package extraction must preserve stable sourceRef/provenance/error semantics and existing callers during migration.
Research must identify exact import/export/package changes and compatibility seam before worker execution.
successCriteria: A package/module topology is specified where Oracle is infrastructure-owned and Agentic Application consumes it through explicit concrete seams.
Backend and QA concrete context resolution behavior remains semantically unchanged after extraction.
No generic resolver/provider framework is required unless separate evidence proves pressure beyond the two concrete source classes.
